exposure: Global perinatal asphyxia (induced by immersing foetus-containing uterine horns in a water bath at 37°C for 21 min)
cohort: The study participants were term rat foetuses delivered by caesarean section, divided into an asphyxia-exposed group and sibling control foetuses.
finding: Global perinatal asphyxia produced a regionally specific and sustained increase in GSSG/GSH ratio, a decrease in tissue reducing capacity, a decrease of catalase activity, and an increase of cleaved caspase-3 levels in rat brains up to 14 postnatal days, mainly affecting the mesencephalon and hippocampus.
